challenge: Managing 800+ products across an e-commerce store and fashion lookbook manually would be unsustainable. The site required three distinct sections — e-commerce store, fashion lookbook magazine, and editorial content — all pulling from interconnected databases while maintaining separate navigation patterns and checkout integration. Webflow's CMS capabilities combined with Notion and Make.com offered the foundation for a fully automated content and inventory management system.
approach: Architected a fully automated Webflow e-commerce system with custom backend integration. Connected Make.com automation workflows to Notion databases containing product information, fashion imagery, and editorial content, which automatically populate Webflow CMS collections and sync inventory across all storefronts. Designed custom navigation that handles the site's complexity, allowing users to flow between shopping, lookbook, and editorial sections without losing context. When the site was later deployed to GitHub Pages, developed Python utility scripts to correct image paths, navigation links, nested directory handling, and lookbook navigation issues.
result: The automation eliminated manual data entry for 800+ products and reduced inventory update time from hours to minutes. The Make.com integration enabled real-time synchronization between Notion databases, Webflow CMS, and checkout systems. The custom navigation architecture proved robust enough for the multi-section site while remaining intuitive. The Python migration scripts demonstrated full-stack problem-solving beyond Webflow design, addressing real technical challenges in deeply nested directory structures.
skill_summary: Full-stack automation, Webflow CMS, Make.com workflows, Notion database management, Python scripting, and e-commerce architecture.

process.summary: Audit existing workflows, identify manual bottlenecks, and map where AI tooling or custom automation will deliver the highest leverage.
Build iteratively — custom scripts, AI-generated SERP descriptions, Webflow storefronts connected to inventory APIs. Ship early, validate with real traffic.
Monitor performance, A/B test conversion paths, continuously refine. The goal: a system that runs autonomously, not a one-time build.
